briefing.text: These tables are TCGA cutaneous melanoma (SKCM). data_clinical_sample.txt already has a MUTATION_TYPE column with values Triple_WT (n=46), BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants (150), RAS_Hotspot_Mutants (92), NF1_Any_Mutants (28) and NA (43). The hypothesis is therefore about this study's own subtypes. There is no copy-number table, but that alone does not make the claim Not verifiable under the benchmark convention. Test the KIT part with the mutation table and judge the focal-amplification part from established melanoma biology, stating which kind of evidence decided each part.
briefing.reason: This stops the team from wrongly answering Not verifiable just because there is no CNA file. It also points them to the subtype variable that already exists.

briefing.text: Use the provided MUTATION_TYPE column to define the subtypes, and drop the 43 NA samples. Do not re-derive the groups from the MAF. The study used a hierarchy (BRAF hotspot, then RAS hotspot, then NF1 any, else triple-WT), and your own calls may not match it. If you do re-derive them, cross-tabulate against MUTATION_TYPE.
briefing.reason: If the team builds its own groups, the comparison may not be the one the study made.

briefing.text: data_mutations.txt (274 MB) contains silent, intronic, UTR and other non-coding calls. For KIT (Hugo_Symbol==KIT), keep only protein-altering classes: Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame and Splice_Site. Count samples, not rows, so each sample with at least one such mutation counts once. Match Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID.
briefing.reason: Counting every row inflates and distorts KIT mutation rates.

briefing.text: The BRAF, RAS and especially NF1 subtypes are UV-hypermutated, so they carry many passenger KIT mutations. Split KIT mutations by subtype into known drivers (exon 11, e.g. W557 or L576P; exon 13 K642E; exon 17 D816 or N822) and other mutations, and compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS across subtypes. Base the enrichment test on known-driver or recurrent KIT mutations, or adjust any-KIT-mutation status for log TMB with logistic regression. Do not rely on raw counts alone.
briefing.reason: Raw KIT mutation rates are confounded by mutational burden and can reverse the apparent direction of enrichment.

briefing.text: There are only 46 Triple_WT tumours and few KIT mutants. Build the 2x2 table (Triple_WT vs other subtypes, by KIT-mutant status) and use Fisher's exact test. Report the per-group percentages and the odds ratio with its confidence interval. Judge the direction and size of the effect; a non-significant p-value alone is not evidence against enrichment.
briefing.reason: With so few cases, chi-square is unreliable and a strict p<0.05 rule could mislead the label.

briefing.text: data_mutsig.txt gives cohort-wide MutSig significance per gene and has no subtype column. A significant KIT result there shows only that KIT is a recurrent driver in the cohort, not that it is enriched in Triple_WT.
briefing.reason: This keeps the team from using the wrong table as evidence of subtype enrichment.

briefing.text: ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY (if present) measures whole-genome ploidy, not focal amplification. Do not let a ploidy difference between subtypes, or the lack of one, decide the focal-amplification part of the claim. Judge that part from established literature on triple-WT (non-BRAF/RAS/NF1) cutaneous melanoma, which discusses focal amplifications at loci such as 4q12 (KIT/PDGFRA/KDR), CDK4, CCND1, MDM2 and TERT.
briefing.reason: This prevents a proxy variable that measures the wrong thing from being used to judge the focal-amplification part of the claim.

briefing.text: The hypothesis has two parts: KIT mutation enrichment and focal amplifications. Report each separately: what the data show for KIT in Triple_WT versus the other subtypes, and what biology says about focal amplifications. Do not label the claim False only because one part cannot be measured directly. Call it False only if a testable part clearly goes against the claim (for example, KIT driver mutations being rarer in Triple_WT than in the other subtypes).
briefing.reason: This affects how the evidence from the two parts is combined into one label.

shared_assumptions: Both teams treat the study's MUTATION_TYPE label as the definition of Triple_WT and drop the 43 NA samples without checking whether any NA samples carry KIT mutations or would fall into Triple_WT by the stated hierarchy.
Both teams treat each sample as an independent unit and compare Triple_WT against all other subtypes pooled, without reporting per-subtype rates or checking one sample per patient.
Both teams take the focal-amplification half from recollection of the source study and assume it agrees with the claim; neither tested it, and neither looked for any proxy in the tables.
unused_evidence: UV_SIGNATURE / UV_RATE (patient table): the two teams adjust only for TMB. A UV-low share in Triple_WT would show the group is biologically distinct (in line with KIT drivers), but neither team checked how it is spread across subtypes.
ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY, SAMPLE_TYPE and REGIONAL_VS_PRIMARY (sample table): never used, so no one checked whether primary and metastatic samples are mixed differently across subtypes.
Sample IDs with suffixes other than -01 (e.g. -06 metastases), and whether any patient has more than one sample.
data_mutsig.txt: used only as context; it could still confirm that KIT counts as a significant driver gene in the cohort.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the focal-amplification part as their weakest point and only reported it. Neither team resolved it, and neither said how sure it is of the literature claim or which loci it relies on.

Team B's any-nonsilent comparison did not account for TMB or separate hotspot mutations from passengers; Team A did both. Team B did not reconcile its counts with Team A's driver counts (5/270 vs 3/270).
second_readings: 'Focal amplifications' could mean focal amplification of KIT itself (4q12) or a general excess of focal amplifications/structural complexity in Triple_WT. These are different claims, and the teams did not say which one they judged.
'Enrichment' could be judged against each other subtype separately or against all of them pooled. Against NF1 alone (3/28 KIT mutants), enrichment may be weak.
challenge.verdict: Moderate-to-high trust. The KIT part is directly supported, and it holds up under driver restriction and TMB adjustment (Team A). The focal-amplification part rests only on both teams' shared memory of the literature, and neither team tested it or said how sure it is.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate known-driver KIT mutations separately for each subtype (BRAF, RAS, NF1, Triple_WT) and for the 43 NA samples. Is Triple_WT enriched against NF1 alone, not only against the pooled groups? Do any KIT driver mutants sit in the dropped NA group, and does either result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Check whether any patient has more than one sample, and how SAMPLE_TYPE (primary/metastatic) is spread across subtypes. Does restricting to one sample per patient change the KIT result?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For the focal-amplification part, write down which loci and which comparison you believe the source study reported for Triple_WT, and how sure you are. Do you read the claim as KIT-locus amplification or as focal amplifications in general, and does the reading change your label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Split your non-silent KIT mutations into known hotspot/driver sites and other sites, and refit with log TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS (and/or UV_SIGNATURE) as a covariate. Does the Triple_WT enrichment survive, and does your method change?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Report KIT mutation rates for each subtype and for the 43 unlabelled samples. Is any comparison against a single subtype (e.g. NF1) not enriched, or do unlabelled samples carry KIT mutations? Does that change how you handle them?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your amplification judgement relies on the source study. Which focal amplifications (loci) do you recall it reporting for Triple_WT versus the other subtypes, and how sure are you? Would a reading of 'focal amplifications' as KIT-locus amplification specifically change your label?

In large cutaneous melanoma genomic classifications into BRAF, RAS, NF1 and triple-wild-type subtypes, which subtype shows a higher frequency of focal amplifications, and which loci (e.g. KIT/PDGFRA/KDR at 4q12, CDK4, CCND1, MDM2, TERT) are reported?
questions.why: Both teams decided the untested focal-amplification half from memory alone; an independent check would confirm or overturn it.

questions.question: Which KIT mutation positions are considered recurrent oncogenic drivers in melanoma (exons 11, 13, 17), and how often are KIT mutations in UV-hypermutated melanomas passengers?
questions.why: This settles whether the teams' driver/passenger split of KIT mutations is correct, which bears on the enrichment estimate.

findings.question: In large cutaneous melanoma genomic classifications into BRAF, RAS, NF1 and triple-wild-type subtypes, which subtype shows a higher frequency of focal amplifications, and which loci (e.g. KIT/PDGFRA/KDR at 4q12, CDK4, CCND1, MDM2, TERT) are reported?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: every search/contents call failed (HTTP 403 from the search provider; PubMed link blocked). From domain knowledge: the TCGA SKCM classification (Cell 2015) reported that Triple-WT tumours have more focal amplifications and copy-number/structural complexity than the BRAF, RAS and NF1 subtypes. The recurrent focal amplifications include 4q12 (KIT/PDGFRA/KDR), CDK4, CCND1, MDM2 and TERT. This supports the focal-amplification half of the hypothesis.

From domain knowledge: the TCGA SKCM classification (Cell 2015) reported that Triple-WT tumours have more focal amplifications and copy-number/structural complexity than the BRAF, RAS and NF1 subtypes. The recurrent focal amplifications include 4q12 (KIT/PDGFRA/KDR), CDK4, CCND1, MDM2 and TERT. This supports the focal-amplification half of the hypothesis. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

findings.question: Which KIT mutation positions are considered recurrent oncogenic drivers in melanoma (exons 11, 13, 17), and how often are KIT mutations in UV-hypermutated melanomas passengers?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the web tool was unavailable (HTTP 403). From domain knowledge, the driver hotspots are: exon 11 (L576P is the most common; also W557R, V559A/D, and indels at K550-K558), exon 13 (K642E), exon 17 (D816H/V, D820Y, N822K/Y) and exon 18 (A829P). In UV-hypermutated BRAF, RAS and NF1 tumours, KIT mutations outside these hotspots are mostly scattered UV-signature (C>T) passengers, probably most of the KIT calls in those groups, but I could not check an exact fraction. Test enrichment on hotspot (driver) KIT mutations, or adjust for TMB. TCGA reported KIT alterations as enriched in Triple-WT.
